input.rationale: Advance the audit on an executable, scheduling-independent relationship: the runtime's decided-stream cursor advances one step per element returned by read_decided_suffix, but the core collapses a trimmed prefix into a single element. A new investigation is registered and a focused two-node in-process probe is requested to establish the core's returned shape (and the resulting cursor replay) from actual retained execution.

investigations.question: When a DecidedSub starts below the compacted index, does its per-element cursor arithmetic stay index-aligned with read_decided_suffix, or does it re-deliver already-emitted entries on later pushes?
investigations.hypothesis: The core returns one Trimmed/Snapshotted element in place of the whole trimmed prefix, so the vector is shorter than decided-from. push_to_sub increments next_idx once per element and push_to_all_subs assumes entries[i] is the entry at min_next+i, so after a catch-up that crosses a compaction boundary the cursor lands short of decided and later pushes re-deliver the entries after the compacted index, violating the documented in-order decided stream that applications use to apply entries once.
investigations.discriminator: The actual element count and kinds of read_decided_suffix(from) for from below versus at the compacted index on a real trimmed log, and the first later push computed from the resulting cursor.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading gives a concrete mechanism. In InternalStorage::read, when from is below the compacted index the result is one create_compacted_entry element followed by one element per entry from compacted_idx to the requested end, so for from < compacted_idx the vector has fewer elements than decided_idx - from; the Trimmed(t)/Snapshotted variant is a marker for the whole trimmed prefix, not one index. The runtime stores only next_idx per subscriber, increments it once per element pushed (push_to_sub and push_to_all_subs), and push_to_all_subs computes start = sub.next_idx - min_next assuming one element per index. A subscription or catch-up at from < compacted therefore ends with next_idx = from + 1 + (decided - compacted), short of decided, and the next push re-reads from that cursor and re-sends entries after the compacted index. subscribe_decided accepts any from and documents a single in-order stream; nothing rejects or compensates for a compacted starting index. The retained execution is needed to pin the core's returned shape (element count and kinds) and the resulting replay; the claim remains unresolved until that receipt is associated.
counterevidence: If the caller only ever subscribes at or above the compacted index, read_decided_suffix returns exactly one element per index and the cursor arithmetic is aligned; the defect is limited to a starting or lagging cursor below compaction.
A Trimmed/Snapshotted marker is a documented LogEntry variant, so delivering it is not itself wrong; the defect is the cursor advance that treats the marker as one index.
limitations: omnipaxos_runtime is not a dev-dependency of the omnipaxos test target, so the actor itself cannot be compiled or run from the assurance harness; only the core read shape can be executed here.
The probe reproduces the actor's cursor arithmetic over real core outputs; that reproduction is a reconstruction of source logic, not an execution of the runtime crate.
The scenario uses in-memory storage without snapshots and a single compaction point; snapshot-based compaction and concurrent multi-subscriber reads are not exercised.

scope.description: Two real OmniPaxos instances (pids 1 and 2) in one process, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots; node 1 becomes leader via try_become_leader, six entries are appended and decided, then the leader trims to index 4. The probe records read_decided_suffix(1) and (4) shapes and replays the actor's cursor arithmetic from source over those real outputs.
assumptions: All messages produced by either instance are delivered synchronously to their addressed node until no message remains (reliable, ordered, no loss).
Only local calls append, try_become_leader and trim drive the run; no ticks, so BLE elections do not occur.
Trim(4) is accepted because the leader's minimum accepted index is 6 for both nodes.
excluded: Network faults, reconnect handling, snapshots, batching, reconfiguration and concurrent client calls.

experiment.prefix: Build both nodes from ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2]} and default ServerConfig with pid 1/2 and MemoryStorage. Pump until quiescent, call node1.try_become_leader(), pump until leader state is (pid 1, Accept). Append Value(1..=6) with a full pump after each append so every entry is decided on both nodes. Call node1.trim(Some(4)) and pump; node 2 applies the forwarded Trim(4). Emit CA_EVENT ready (leader_is_1_accept, decided, decided_peer, compacted), then suffix_shape events for from=1 and from=4 (from, decided, compacted, len, decided_minus_from, kinds, tokens), then cursor_replay: start cursor at 1, apply push_to_sub's for-each-element next_idx += 1 to read_decided_suffix(cursor), then apply one later push_to_all_subs read from the resulting cursor with start=0, and report catchup_tokens, cursor_after_catchup, next_push_tokens, delivered_values, duplicate_values, duplicates, decided.

comparisons.description: Requesting from index 1 below compacted 4 returns the compacted marker plus the two remaining entries, so len is 3 while decided_minus_from is 5.
Requesting from the compacted boundary itself returns one element per remaining index (len 2).
The per-element cursor after catch-up is short of decided, so the next push re-delivers entries 5 and 6.

investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a legal actor schedule lets the origin process the new ballot and the decided advance to idx before any drain_notifiers pass observes the stale pending (the false Ok is avoided if a tick drains while decided < idx, yielding Superseded), and whether the decided entry at idx is the replacement rather than the caller's entry.

gaps.question: Is there a reachable actor schedule in which the originating node observes the new ballot and decided_idx >= assigned_idx within one drain_notifiers pass, so that the Ok arm preempts Superseded and the entry at idx is the replacement entry?

interpretations.rationale: The source establishes the mechanism: a pending append_notify stores only (assigned_idx, assignment_ballot), and drain_notifiers resolves Ok whenever decided_idx >= assigned_idx before it checks whether that ballot has been superseded; nothing in the Ok path reads the entry at assigned_idx. The runtime's own tests establish both premises the false Ok would need: Ok(idx) is expected to mean the caller's value is decided at idx, and an entry accepted only on the old leader can be replaced at the same index by a different decided value while the origin learns of the new ballot. What is not yet established is the decisive schedule: the origin's actor drains on each tick (10 ms by default) and when commands arrive, so a drain while decided_idx < assigned_idx and the promise ballot has already changed yields Superseded and avoids the false Ok. A false Ok requires the decided advance to assigned_idx and the ballot change to be visible in the same drain pass, or the decided advance to arrive with the new ballot before any intervening tick. The runtime crate is not a dev-dependency of the omnipaxos test target, so the fixed assurance_generated harness cannot execute this path; the open question is therefore the actor-level interleaving and log-content identity, not the core Paxos decision rule.
counterevidence: The Superseded doc explicitly calls itself a heuristic and notes the entry can still be decided under the new ballot at log_entry_idx; when the caller's entry survives reconciliation, returning Ok once decided_idx reaches idx is correct and must not be suppressed.

The false-Ok case requires the origin's own minority-accepted entry to be replaced at that index; if the new leader adopts the value, the decided entry at idx is still the caller's entry and Ok is accurate.
limitations: omnipaxos_runtime is not listed in omnipaxos/Cargo.toml dev-dependencies, so tests/assurance_generated.rs in the omnipaxos crate cannot construct the actor or call append_notify.
No execution receipt exists for this question; the account rests on source reading and the runtime's saved test expectations, which describe intent but do not establish a schedule.

The hash-free timing of tokio channel delivery and the actor's select_biased loop is unmeasured here; the 10 ms tick and 1 ms egress defaults in RuntimeConfig are configuration, not observed interleaving.

result.summary: Registered a second, scheduling-independent investigation: the runtime's per-element decided-stream cursor versus the core's collapse of a trimmed prefix into one LogEntry element. Added seven source anchors (InternalStorage::read/get_entry_type/create_compacted_entry, DecidedSub, push_to_sub, push_to_all_subs, subscribe_decided), an unresolved source-level account of the under-advance and later re-delivery, and requested one focused two-node in-process experiment at omnipaxos/tests/assurance_generated.rs that decides six entries, trims to 4, records read_decided_suffix(1) and (4) shapes, and replays the actor's cursor arithmetic over those real outputs. No receipt yet; the defect claim stays unresolved until the execution is interpreted. Prior append_notify question remains active with its gap unaddressed.
